title: Unbounded tombstone accumulation in ShortAddressCoordinator
description:
[codereview]

## Location
`python/src/lichen/link/address_assignment.py` lines 604-608, 371-380

## Summary
When peers release their addresses, tombstone entries (EUI64 -> last_sequence) are created to prevent DAO sequence replay attacks. These tombstones are never automatically cleaned up.

## Failure Scenario
1. Coordinator starts with lease-based address management
2. Many peers join and later release their addresses (via AssignmentOperation.RELEASE)
3. Each release creates a tombstone entry in `_last_sequence_by_eui` but NOT in `_expires_by_eui`
4. `prune_expired()` only removes entries that have expiries; tombstones have no expiry
5. Over time, tombstone count grows toward the limit of 65533 (SHORT_POOL_SIZE)
6. Memory usage grows: ~9 bytes per tombstone = ~600KB worst case

## Analysis
- Line 674-675, 678: On release, sequence is stored but no expiry is set
- Line 589-591: `prune_expired` iterates `_expires_by_eui`, which excludes tombstones
- Line 604-607: Sequences are only removed if the EUI64 is in the `expired` set
- Tombstones are only "cleaned" if the peer allocates again (lines 712-714)

The tombstone limit at line 372 prevents unbounded growth but does not provide cleanup:
```python
if len(tombstone_euis) > _SHORT_POOL_SIZE:
    raise AssignmentProtocolError("too many released-peer sequence tombstones")
```

## Suggested Fix
Add a tombstone TTL or a bounded LRU eviction for released-peer sequences. The security window for replay protection is typically short (minutes to hours), so old tombstones can be safely pruned.
